verses.1: Men, brothers and fathers, please listen to my apology to you now.
verses.2: They heard that the Hebrew man addressed them more gently and with greater calmness. And it is said that…
verses.3: I am a Jew, born in Tarso in Cilicia. I was raised in this same city, under the care of Gamaliel. I was taught according to the laws of my father’s religion. I cherished God as you all do today.
verses.4: Who pursued this path until death came, binding and sending men and women into prisons.
verses.5: Just as the high priest testified to me, so also does the entire council. With them, I also carried letters to my brothers in Damascus. I sent those who were there to Jerusalem, so that they could be punished accordingly.
verses.6: And as I was walking along, around noon, suddenly a bright light appeared from the sky and enveloped me.
verses.7: He fell to the ground, and I heard a voice saying to me, “Saulo, Saul, why do you persecute me?”
verses.8: I replied, “Who are you, Lord?” He said to me, “I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom you are seeking.”
verses.9: But those who were with me saw the light, but they couldn’t hear what I was saying.
verses.10: I said, “What should I do, sir?” The lord replied to me, “Go to Damascus. There, you will be told everything that the Romans have planned for you.”
verses.11: And since I did not disregard the glory of his light, I was led by those around me to Damascus.
verses.12: And there was also a man named Ananias, who testified according to the law before all the Jewish residents.
verses.13: He came to me and said, “Saul, my brother.” I looked at him. And I also looked at him during that time.
verses.14: And he said: “The God of our ancestors has always wanted us to know His will, to see His justice, and to hear the voice that comes from His mouth.”
verses.15: Because he has witnesses who can testify before all people, those whom you have seen and heard about him.
verses.16: And now, what do you intend to do? You will be baptized and confess your sins, calling upon His name.
verses.17: It happened that I was brought down to Jerusalem, and while I was praying in the temple, I hoped that I would be saved.
verses.18: And see that I say this to you: Go away from Jerusalem quickly, for you do not accept my testimony against me.
verses.19: I said, “Lord, they must realize that I am also putting those who believe in you into prison and tormenting them.”
verses.20: And when the blood of your witness, Stephen, was poured out, he also was killed. I too was injured and suffered greatly, while I kept watch over those who were trying to kill him.
verses.21: And he said to me, “Go ahead, for I will send you away to distant nations.”
verses.22: They listened to his words until the end, and they heard their voices saying, “Forbid this man to leave the earth; for it is not right for him to live.”
verses.23: They cried out in pain, their sleeves trembling, and they threw handfuls of sand into the air.
verses.24: The khilarianch ordered that he be brought into the room where the decision would be made. He was told to wait there, so that he could understand why they had spoken to him in such a manner.
verses.25: And as they tried to persuade him, Paul said to the leader of the men, “Is it really right for you to think that a Roman man is something worthy of respect?”
verses.26: When the centurion came before the commander, he said, “What do you intend to do?” For this man was a Roman.
verses.27: When the captain came forward, he said to him, “Tell me, are you a Roman?” He replied, “Yes.”
verses.28: The khilinarch replied, “I have ruled over this city for many years.” Paulos said, “I too was born here.”
verses.29: So, those who would later criticize him immediately rejected him. And the khalip also feared that he was a Roman, and that he was worth twelve thousand coins.
verses.30: At the end, wanting to find out what was the “safe” thing that Jews were accusing him of, he decided to ask the high priests and all those who were present at the meeting. He brought Paul before them.
